opened_sources.result: Opened. IAU defines constellations as bounded sky areas and lists Canes Venatici/CVn, Monoceros/Mon, Serpens/Ser and Capricornus/Cap.
Opened. Supports M51 as the Whirlpool spiral in Canes Venatici, dust/gas arms, pink star-forming regions, blue clusters, and the close NGC 5195 interaction. The page does not name NGC 5194.

Opened. Supports Monoceros, roughly 5,000 light-years, roughly 100 light-years, a giant molecular-cloud edge, young-star radiation causing glow, and hydrogen/dust silhouettes. It identifies the broad background as Digitized Sky Survey and Hubble as the small inset; its color statement applies to the composite context image.
Opened. Supports M16 in Serpens, IC 4703 plus NGC 6611, erosion of pillars by ultraviolet radiation and stellar winds, and infrared visibility of stars forming in the pillars plus background stars.

Opened. Supports M30 as a dense old globular cluster in Capricornus about 28,000 light-years away and gives two blue-straggler mechanisms: near-head-on stellar collisions and binary hydrogen transfer. It does not state the draft's property-diagram or hotter/bluer explanation.

additional_source_checked.result: Opened. NASA/JPL-Caltech explicitly calls Whirlpool/Messier 51 NGC 5194/5195, a pair in Canes Venatici. It is a suitable added citation if the current CVn NGC 5194 wording is retained.
